{{Top}}
{{Quote|Use the comlink? Oh, my! I forgot. I turned it off.|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
[[File:Comlink_1.png|thumb|right|250px|A [[Hush-98 comlink/Legends|Hush-98 comlink]]]]
A '''comlink''' or '''communicator''' was a portable device that transferred voice signals from one location to another.

==Description==
{{Quote|Comlinks only fail when you really need them.|A frustrated [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|SpecForce]] comm specialist|<ref name="RoE">''[[Rules of Engagement: The Rebel SpecForce Handbook]]''</ref>}}
Comlinks came in numerous varieties, though most had the same central systems: a receiver, a transmitter, and a power source. Comlinks were typically small, palm-sized devices for easy transportation and concealment. They often weighed as little as 0.1kg. More advanced models featured encryption routines, frequency search controls, sound reproduction matrices, silence projectors, and built-in ports for data transmission. Some comlinks, such as those used by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], were equipped with complex security devices that prevented unauthorized use. Comlinks were often integrated into helmets, such as those that [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] and later [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] wore. Even [[Droid/Legends|droids]] could have [[Internal comlink|integrated comlinks]].<ref name="Roleplaying Game, Saga Edition">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

[[File:Hoth_Transmitter.jpg|thumb|left|Harsh environments required a reliable comlink with a long range.]]
Without satellite amplification, a standard comlink had a range of about 50 kilometers. This range was decreased drastically in dense urban zones due to the presence of high levels of electromagnetic interference, though this could be circumvented by the use of wired transmission networks. Range and signal strength against interference was primarily dependent upon the power source; correspondingly, comlinks with higher levels of available energy (such as military and vehicle-mounted models) had much longer ranges and less interruption than hand-held civilian models. Between [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], comlinks with standard security enhancements cost 200 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].

[[File:Ear_comlink_full_-_SupplyLines.png|thumb|230x230px|An ear comlink]]
Comlinks were also used aboard [[Starship/Legends|starships]], mainly for short-range communications such as landing/departure clearances and formation commands. For longer-range communications, many starships utilized [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|subspace radios]], which necessitated an even larger power supply.<ref name="The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref>

Certain comlinks also had the ability to track other comlinks, presumably by following a transmission feed between them.

While the typical comlink was handheld, it was also not uncommon for them to be worn in a variety of ways to increase portability, usability, or stealth depending on the situation. In this fashion, comlinks were often worn on the [[Wrist link/Legends|wrist]], on the [[Headset comlink|head]], directly on or in the [[Earbud comlink/Legends|ear]], or even implanted under the [[Subcutaneous comlink|skin]]. [[Police officer/Legends|Police officers]] from the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] used such a handsfree comlink to communicate. It was round and covered the wearer's ear. [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Tan Divo/Legends|Tan Divo]] and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jaller Obrim]] both used one.
